data.title: Novartis is said to be abandoning Ionis heart drug after late-stage trial setback
data.description:
Novartis (NVS) is largely abandoning the development of a heart disease therapy discovered by Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS) after the RNA-targeting therapy failed in a late-stage trial last September, Bloomberg reported on Saturday.

The Swiss drugmaker said in a statement that it will discontinue the development of the monthly injection known as pelacarsen for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, a study testing it in a heart valve disease called calcific aortic valve stenosis will continue.

The company didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

In September, shares of Novartis (NVS) and Ionis (IONS) fell after the pharma giant said that based on topline data, pelacarsen didn’t meet its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 trial called Lp(a)HORIZON for patients with elevated lipoprotein(a), a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

Amgen (AMGN), which is advancing its RNA-targeting therapy olpasiran, in partnership with Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals (ARWR) and Royalty Pharma (RPRX) using a similar Lp(a)-lowering approach, also traded lower in sympathy.

On Saturday, Novartis (NVS) presented full data from Lp(a)HORIZON at the American Heart Association’s scientific sessions in Chicago and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

The data analyzed over a median follow-up of roughly five years confirmed that the antisense oligonucleotide reduced serum Lp(a) levels but without a concomitant reduction in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events such as stroke compared with placebo.

data.title: Real Estate Earnings Scorecard: 40% firms beat revenue estimates, 60% post Y/Y growth
data.description:
The real estate sector saw most companies beating earnings estimates last week, but lagging on the revenue front, with only 60% of them showing an annual revenue growth.

Real Estate Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 10 companies that reported, eight firms (80%) exceeded FFO estimates, while one fell short and one was in line with market expectations. Notably, 7 firms (70%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

Top Line: Of the 10 companies, only 4 firms (40%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 6 of them fell below analyst estimates. Notably, only six firms (60%) reported year-over-year earnings growth, while one was flat and three reported an annual decline.

Let’s take a look at some real estate companies that reported earnings this week:

Realty Income (O) reported Q3 revenue of $1.62B, topping the $1.45B consensus, and an adjusted FFO per share of $1.12, beating the average analyst estimate of $1.10. Q3 same-store rental revenue growth slipped to 1.1% Y/Y vs. 1.2% Y/Y growth in Q2. The net lease REIT now expects full-year adjusted FFO per share at $4.45-$4.46 

Simon Property Group (SPG) posted a Q3 revenue of $1.81B, beating the $1.66B consensus, and a real estate FFO per share of $3.37, exceeding the Visible Alpha estimate of $3.29. The company now expects 2026 real estate FFO per share of $13.30-$13.40 (midpoint $13.35) vs. the Visible Alpha consensus of $13.29.

Iron Mountain (IRM) delivered stronger-than-expected Q3 revenue of $1.99B as its growth businesses of data center, digital, and asset lifecycle management, together, grew more than 30% Y/Y. Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $1.53, beating the Visible Alpha consensus of $1.48. The company expects Q4 revenue of ~$2.03B, vs. the average analyst estimate of $2.05B.

data.title: Utilities Earnings Scoreboard: 86% beat EPS estimates, 93% post Y/Y earnings growth
data.description:
Utilities companies delivered largely positive earnings results this week, with most S&P 500 utilities reporting higher earnings year over year. Revenue performance was less uniform, as several companies missed analyst expectations and three recorded annual declines.

Utilities Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 14 companies reporting, 12 firms (86%) topped EPS estimates, 1 met expectations, and 1 missed consensus. On a Y/Y basis, 13 companies (93%) recorded earnings growth.

Top Line: Of the 14 companies reporting, 9 firms (64%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 5 came in below analyst estimates. Meanwhile, 11 companies (79%) reported Y/Y revenue growth.

Here is a look at some utilities companies that reported earnings this week:

Southern Company (SO) reported Q3 revenue of $8.84B, up 13.1% Y/Y, exceeding the $8.41B consensus. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.94, beating the $1.58 estimate and increasing from $1.60 in the year-ago quarter.

Duke Energy (DUK) posted Q3 revenue of $9.10B, up 6.6% Y/Y, topping the $8.97B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.99 outperformed the $1.76 estimate, compared with $1.81 a year earlier.

Entergy (ETR) reported Q3 revenue of $4.37B, up 14.6% Y/Y, exceeding the $4.15B consensus. Adjusted EPS rose 29.4% Y/Y to $1.98, beating the $1.55 estimate.

Evergy (EVRG) posted Q3 revenue of $2.10B, up 15.8% Y/Y, compared with the $1.97B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $2.58 outperformed the $2.05 estimate and increased from $2.03 in the year-ago period.

Sempra (SRE) reported Q3 revenue of $3.19B, up 1.3% Y/Y, but below the $3.31B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.40 exceeded the $1.18 estimate, rising from $1.11 a year earlier.

Public Service Enterprise Group (PEG) reported Q3 revenue of $3.02B, down 6.5% Y/Y, and missing the $3.25B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.15 fell short of the $1.20 estimate, although it was slightly higher than $1.13 in the year-ago quarter.

Eversource Energy (ES) posted Q3 revenue of $2.98B, down 7.5% Y/Y and below the $3.15B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $0.92 matched analyst expectations but declined 22.7% from $1.19 a year earlier, making it the only company among the 14 to report lower Y/Y earnings.

PPL (PPL) reported Q3 revenue of $2.50B, up 11.5% Y/Y, beating the $2.42B consensus. Ongoing EPS of $0.54 outperformed the $0.53 estimate, increasing from $0.48 a year earlier.

Earnings next week

In the coming week, investors will turn their attention to upcoming results from Constellation Energy (CEG) and NRG Energy (NRG).

Utilities ETFs: (XLU), (VPU), (IDU), (FUTY), and (RYU).

data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 96% healthcare firms post EPS wins this week
data.description:
It was a major week for healthcare stocks, with 24 out of 60 companies reporting their results. Pharmaceutical heavyweights like Pfizer (PFE), Viatris (VTRS), and Moderna (MRNA) posted broadly positive quarterly results throughout the week.

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) remained flat through the week even as the broader markets took a sharp plunge. In the year so far, the healthcare sector has risen more than 19% compared to a 7% rise in the S&P500 index.

Earnings Roundup

Of the 24 firms that reported earnings this week, 23, or 95.8%, posted better-than-expected EPS, while one missed analysts’ estimate. Notably, 21 firms (87.5%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

On the revenue front, four firms lagged analysts’ consensus while 83.3% or 20 firms posted top lines above expectations. Notably, 18 firms (75%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.

Below is a snapshot of the quarterly print of some major firms in the healthcare sector:

Pfizer (PFE) posted earnings marginally above Wall Street’s estimates at $0.87 per share on revenue of $16.58B, amid less demand for its COVID-19 products. However, the company raised its full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance to a range of $2.95 to $3.05 and hiked the revenue outlook to the range of $62B to $64B. Concurrently, Pfizer also appointed Cecile Guegan as its next chief financial officer and executive vice president.

Viatris (VTRS) posted a mixed performance for Q3 2026 on Thursday, falling short of consensus for revenue while beating earnings guidance as its generics sales for the quarter fell for the first time this year. EPS rose 6% YoY to $0.71 even as revenue remained flat at $3.7B, compared to the prior year. Citing the strong YTD performance, Viatris raised its full-year guidance ranges for revenue and adjusted EPS to $14.70B - $14.90B and $2.56 - $2.63, respectively.

Moderna (MRNA) shares bounced back after days of decline after the firm posted better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and lifted its full-year growth outlook, citing higher COVID vaccine sales in its overseas markets. It reported earnings of $0.38 per share for the quarter on revenue of $1.3B. Speaking about its cancer vaccine, Moderna said it remains on track to submit regulatory filings for intismeran autogene developed with Merck (MRK) and initiate its commercial launch, subject to regulatory approval.

Out of the pharma companies that reported earnings this week, three were biotechnology firms, and three were pharmaceutical companies. Seven of those belonged to the health care equipment industry, and another seven to the health care providers & services industry, while four came from life sciences tools & services.

Upcoming Earnings

With the earnings season drawing to a close, only one major healthcare firm, Hims & Hers Health (HIMS), is due to report its results next week.

data.title: J&J posts late-stage trial win for plaque psoriasis pill in psoriatic arthritis
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) announced on Saturday that Icotyde, its FDA-approved therapy marketed with Protagonist Therapeutics (PTGX) for plaque psoriasis, succeeded in a late-stage trial for psoriatic arthritis.

With studies showing that up to 30% of patients with plaque PsO also develop PsA, the positive outcome of the company’s Phase 3 ICONIC-PsA 1 represents another medical use for the interleukin-23 receptor antagonist.

In March, the FDA licensed Icotyde for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in those aged 12 years and older at a time when additional trials, including ICONIC-PsA 1 for the once-daily pill, were ongoing.

At a rheumatology event on Saturday, J&J (JNJ) said that ICONIC-PsA 1 met its primary endpoint, with 58% of patients on Icotyde at Week 16 achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20) response, which indicates 20% or more improvement in disease activity.

In comparison, 41% on placebo achieved ACR20. 29% and 13% also achieved ACR50 and ACR70, indicating ≥50% and ≥70% improvement, respectively, compared with 16% and 5% over the same period.

There were no new safety signals associated with Icotyde, with the treatment showing a tolerability profile consistent with its established safety profile, according to J&J (JNJ). The randomized trial enrolled biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis.

"These new findings underscore the potential of ICOTYDE to meaningfully improve outcomes in psoriatic arthritis and add to the growing body of evidence across psoriatic disease,” said David Lee, JNJ’s Global Immunology Therapeutic Area Head.

data.title: S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary Earnings: 89% beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
S&P 500 consumer discretionary (XLY) companies delivered a largely positive earnings performance this week, with the majority beating analyst expectations on both earnings and revenue. However, year-over-year growth was more mixed, with six of the nine reporting companies posting increases in both EPS and sales.

S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the nine companies reporting this week, eight (89%) exceeded EPS expectations, while one fell short. Notably, six firms (67%) posted year-over-year EPS growth.

Top Line: Of the nine companies reporting, seven (78%) exceeded revenue expectations, while two (22%) missed analyst estimates. Notably, six firms (67%) reported year-over-year revenue growth.

Here’s a look at some of the consumer discretionary firms that reported earnings this week:

Airbnb (ABNB) beat on both the top- and bottom-line with 19% revenue growth and a profit of $3.16 per share coming in better than Wall Street expected. Gross booking value rose 21% to an above consensus $27.7B, while the average daily rate for a booking increased by 4% to $179, exceeding $177.14 estimates. Third quarter adjusted EBITDA improved by 19% to an above-consensus $2.5B.

Booking (BKNG) reported an adjusted profit of $4.66 per share, up 17% year-over-year and 17 cents above expectations. Revenue was adjusted by $900M related to a matter associated with the Federal Trade Commission. Excluding this impact, revenue increased 9% to $9.8B, beating the consensus estimate of $9.54B.

Wynn Resorts (WYNN) reported a below consensus adjusted EPS of $0.33, with revenue falling 7.7% to $1.69B, which also missed estimates by $60M.

Yum! Brands (YUM) reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.56, which was above the $1.51 Bloomberg consensus. Revenue was $2.06B, compared with the $2.07B estimate. Growth at KFC helped offset weaker comparable sales at Taco Bell. KFC recorded 1% comparable-sales growth and a 6% increase in system sales excluding currency effects. Its reported operating profit rose 9% to $425M. Taco Bell's comparable sales fell 4%, and system sales declined 2%.

Consumer Discretionary ETFs: (XLY), (VCR), (FXD), (FDIS), (RSPD), and (RXI).

data.title: Financials Earnings Scorecard: 87% beat EPS estimates; Y/Y earnings growth mixed
data.description:
Financial stocks took center stage this week as investors digested a wave of third-quarter earnings from major sector leaders.

The Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) continues to lag the broader market, posting a 4.57% year-to-date gain against a 7.43% rally for the S&P 500 Index.

Across this week’s earnings roundup, 15 financial companies reported results, delivering a strong beat rate against Wall Street expectations for both top- and bottom-line figures. However, Y/Y results were more mixed, as profit growth generally lagged revenue expansion across the group.

Financial Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 15 financial companies with analyst estimates, 13 beat non-GAAP EPS estimates, one missed and one came in line, resulting in an 86.7% beat rate. On a Y/Y basis, across all 16 companies, nine (56.3%) reported Y/Y EPS growth.

Top Line: Of the 15 financial companies, 11 beat revenue expectations and four missed, resulting in a 73.3% beat rate. On a Y/Y basis, 13 of the 16 companies (81.3%) reported revenue growth. Loews (L), which had no analyst consensus estimates, was excluded from the beat-rate calculation.

Let’s take a look at some financial sector companies that reported earnings this week:

Block (XYZ) reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.13, beating estimates by $0.10, while revenue rose 10% Y/Y to $6.72B, topping expectations by $120M. Growth was supported by a 22% increase in gross profit to $3.24B, with Square gross profit up 14%. Adjusted operating income surged 92% to $923M. Management raised its 2026 outlook and expects at least 15% gross profit growth in 2027.

Allstate (ALL) posted non-GAAP EPS of $9.76, beating estimates by $2.80, while revenue increased 0.6% Y/Y to $17.35B but missed forecasts by $110M. Its Property-Liability combined ratio was 86.6%, with higher catastrophe losses adding 7.1 percentage points. The insurer returned $1.5B to shareholders during the quarter and said it plans to launch sales-related AI capabilities in early 2027.

Prudential Financial (PRU) reported non-GAAP EPS of $3.77, beating estimates by $0.45, while revenue declined 16.9% Y/Y to $13.49B, missing forecasts by $672M. AUM remained broadly stable at $1.616T, compared with $1.612T in the prior-year quarter.

Fiserv (FISV) delivered non-GAAP EPS of $1.75, beating estimates by $0.04, while revenue fell 1.4% Y/Y to $4.85B but topped expectations. Organic revenue was flat, with Merchant Solutions down 2% and Financial Solutions up 2%.

CEO Takis Georgakopoulos said revenue had stabilized after the second-quarter trough and expected Merchant revenue to return to growth in the fourth quarter. Fiserv also reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.20–$7.40.

American International Group (AIG) posted non-GAAP EPS of $2.06, beating estimates by $0.18, while revenue increased 17.2% Y/Y to $7.44B, exceeding expectations by $28.9M. The firm returned $787M to shareholders, including $527M in buybacks, and expected the full-year 2026 General Insurance expense ratio to be approximately 30.5%.

Aflac (AFL) reported EPS of $2.43, beating estimates by $0.63, while revenue fell 2.6% Y/Y to $4.30B but topped expectations by $90M. EPS declined 2.4% from a year earlier, indicating that the earnings beat did not translate into Y/Y growth.

MetLife (MET) delivered non-GAAP EPS of $2.78, beating estimates by $0.01, while revenue rose 11.2% Y/Y to $19.91B but missed estimates by $63.7M. Adjusted EPS increased 22% to $2.85, supported in part by $720M in variable investment income. CEO Michel Khalaf called it the company's highest adjusted EPS quarter.

Other Financial Companies

The remaining companies also posted mostly positive results. Assurant (AIZ), Franklin Resources (BEN), Corpay (CPAY), Fidelity National Information Services (FIS), and Jack Henry & Associates (JKHY) beat both EPS and revenue estimates.

Meanwhile, Global Payments (GPN) met EPS expectations and narrowly beat revenue estimates by approximately $267K, while Apollo Global Management (APO) missed EPS expectations but exceeded revenue forecasts.

Loews (L) reported EPS of $1.50 and revenue of $4.76B; compared with the prior-year period, EPS fell 38.3% while revenue increased 1.9% Y/Y.

Overall, the sector's results showed stronger revenue growth than earnings growth.

Earnings ahead: Investors will watch KKR & Co. (KKR), which is scheduled to report its results next week.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: AMD, Qualcomm and Lumentum in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week amid a persistent sell-off from investors and earnings reports from companies including Qualcomm and AMD.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the green on Friday, leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

Fiserv (FISV) +25.71%

First Solar (FSLR) +15.33%

Corpay (CPAY) +13.47%

Block (XYZ) +12.16%

Jack Henry & Associates (JKHY) +7.37%

Top Losers:

Lumentum (LITE) -35.94%

Seagate Technology (STX) -28.48%

Marvell Technology (MRVL) -28.11%

Western Digital (WDC) -27.95%

Sandisk (SNDK) -27.44%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Qualcomm crash following Q4 results

Qualcomm (QCOM) shares plunged after its smartphone chip revenue tumbled 26% in the fourth quarter as rising memory prices weighed on handset demand.

The San Diego-based semiconductor offered mixed guidance that overshadowed results for the fiscal fourth quarter. For the period ending Sept. 27, Qualcomm said it earned an adjusted $2.17 per share as revenue fell 7% year-over-year to come in at $10.44B.

Wall Street analysts have lowered their price targets on the stock given margin pressures and continued Apple modem share losses as risks to its near-term outlook.

Marvell announces $115B all-stock deal for Lumentum

Following speculation that a deal could be announced soon, Marvell Technology (MRVL) disclosed that it intends to acquire Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock deal. The deal puts an enterprise value of $115B on Lumentum, or roughly $1,132 per share. 

According to Bloomberg, before announcing the deal, CEOs of both Marvell and Lumentum asked Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang’s opinion on the proposed deal, following which Huang gave his blessing on the potential tie-up, as consolidation among crucial suppliers in the AI buildout could reduce bottlenecks.

AMD in focus after better-than-expected results, guidance

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) closed nearly 4% higher in extended trading on Tuesday as the semiconductor giant reported third-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast. This also led to Wall Street praising the company's data center strength.

Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore said the company is taking advantage of stronger server market conditions and taking “meaningful” share from companies like Intel.

AMD also recorded a third-quarter charge of more than $1B tied to the performance-based stock warrants it issued to major AI customers OpenAI (OPENAI) and Meta Platforms (META). The chipmaker struck deals with OpenAI and Meta, agreeing to supply them chips in exchange for warrants that could let them buy up to 10% ​of AMD if it meets certain milestones.

However, the stock closed over 17% lower on Thursday following a broader tech sell-off.

Micron Technology plunges amid chip selloff, Taiwan plant halt

Micron Technology (MU) has suspended plans for a memory chip plant in Taiwan amid a prolonged labor dispute, raising uncertainty over a major production base for components used in artificial intelligence systems, Bloomberg reported.

Micron dropped more than 17% on Thursday amid a sweeping semiconductor and AI-stock selloff, with reports linking the broader weakness to investor concerns about political scrutiny potentially slowing data-center development and infrastructure spending.

In other news, Cisco (CSCO) was downgraded to Equal-Weight from Overweight at Morgan Stanley on Thursday, as the investment firm said concerns are growing ahead of the networking giant's earnings, set to be released on Nov. 12.

HP (HPQ) disclosed that it has appointed former GSK (GSK) CEO Emma Walmsley as its new CEO. Walmsley will take over for interim CEO Bruce Broussard, who has been in the top spot since February.
